tuya_account.title: Create the developer account
tuya_account.intro: It is free and you only do it once. OpenLight uses it just to read each bulb's local key; after that everything works without the cloud.
steps: Go to iot.tuya.com and click “Sign Up”.
Use your email (it can be the same as Smart Life, but it doesn't have to).
Confirm the code you get by email.
If it asks for the account type, choose “Individual developer”.
tuya_account.tip: The portal changes often. If something doesn't match this guide, look for a button with a similar name.

cloud_project.title: Create the Cloud project
cloud_project.intro: The project is what gives you the Access ID and Access Secret OpenLight asks for.
steps: In the left menu: Cloud → Development.
Click “Create Cloud Project”.
Use any name (for example “OpenLight”).
Industry: “Smart Home”. Development Method: “Smart Home”.
Data Center: the one matching your Smart Life account (see “Choose the Data Center”).
Accept the suggested services (“IoT Core” must be there).
The project's “Overview” tab shows the Access ID and Access Secret.
cloud_project.tip: If the Access Secret is mistyped, Tuya answers “sign invalid”. Use the portal's copy button.

data_center.title: Choose the Data Center
data_center.intro: It must be where your Smart Life account lives, which depends on the country you picked when you created it.
steps: In Smart Life: Me → Settings → Account and Security → Region. That is your country.
Americas: “Western America”. Europe: “Central Europe”. India: “India”. China: “China”.
If unsure, pick any: OpenLight tries the others and tells you the right one.
data_center.tip: You can change the project's Data Center later in Overview → Edit.

link_smart_life.title: Link Smart Life
link_smart_life.intro: This lets the project see the bulbs you already added in the phone app.
steps: In the project: “Devices” tab → “Link App Account” (or “Link Tuya App Account”).
Click “Add App Account”: a QR code appears.
On your phone, open Smart Life → Me → the scan icon (top right).
Scan the QR and confirm. Your account and bulbs show up in the portal.
link_smart_life.tip: If Tuya says “permission denied”, this step is almost always missing or the Data Center is not your account's.

iot_core_trial.title: Extend the IoT Core trial
iot_core_trial.intro: The free IoT Core trial expires every few months. It is only needed to add bulbs or renew keys: daily use is 100% local.
steps: Go to iot.tuya.com → Cloud → Cloud Services.
Find “IoT Core” and open it.
Click “Extend Trial Period” (or “Renew”), fill in the form and wait for approval (usually automatic).

device_troubleshooting.title: The bulb doesn't respond
device_troubleshooting.intro: It is almost always one of these four things.
steps: The computer and the bulb must be on the same Wi-Fi (watch out for “guest” or separate 5 GHz networks).
Close the Smart Life app on your phone: it sometimes holds the bulb's local connection.
If the bulb was turned off at the wall switch, turn it on and wait 10 seconds.
If you re-paired it in Smart Life, the key changed: use “Renew key”.
device_troubleshooting.tip: Diagnostics shows the exact reason for each bulb's last disconnect.

permissions.title: System permissions
permissions.intro: OpenLight needs to see the screen and talk to the bulbs on your network. Nothing leaves your computer.
steps: macOS: System Settings → Privacy & Security → Screen Recording → enable OpenLight. Then reopen the app: macOS requires it.
macOS: if Screen Recording shows as on but nothing works (common after an update), choose “Repair permission”, turn it on again and reopen the app.
macOS: in the same section, “Local Network” → enable OpenLight.
Windows: if the firewall prompt appears, allow “Private networks”.
Linux (Wayland): when the desktop asks which screen to share, choose the monitor. OpenLight remembers the choice.

tuya_account.lead: Tuya is the company behind Smart Life. Its developer portal is the only official way to read your bulbs' local key.
steps: Open iot.tuya.com and create a free account (email and password).
Confirm the code you get by email.
If asked, choose “Individual developer”.

cloud_project.lead: A Cloud project is your own “app” inside the portal. It gives you the two keys you paste in step 6.
steps: Left menu: Cloud → Development → “Create Cloud Project”.
Name: anything. Industry and Development Method: “Smart Home”.
Data Center: your Smart Life account's (choose it below).
Accept the suggested services; “IoT Core” must be there.
cloud_project.note: IoT Core comes with a free trial that expires every few months. That's fine: it is only needed to add bulbs or renew keys, and it can be extended for free.

link_app.lead: Link your Smart Life account to the project so it can see your bulbs.
steps: In the project: “Devices” tab → “Link App Account”.
“Add App Account”: a QR shows up on screen.
phone_steps: Open Smart Life on your phone.
Tap the scan icon (top right) and point at the QR.
Confirm: your bulbs show up in the portal.

credentials.lead: In the project, “Overview” tab: copy the Access ID and Access Secret (the copy button avoids typos).
credentials.note: The keys are stored in the system keychain, never in a text file.
